blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = -\sin 2x,\ x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh graph banane ka sawal hai. \(y = -\sin 2x\) asal mein sine ki lehar hai, jise 2 ne daba diya (chakkar jaldi poora hota hai) aur minus ne ulta (upside down) kar diya.
Plan: amplitude aur period nikalenge, ek period \([0, \pi]\) ki table banayenge, phir usi pattern ko \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) par 4 dafa dohrayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = -\sin 2x\), \(x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
Humein banana hai: is interval par graph.
Tareeqa: pehle amplitude (lehar ki unchai) aur period (ek chakkar ki lambai) nikalenge. Phir period ke chauthe hisse (quarter period) ke faasle par x-values lenge, kyunke inhi jagahon par graph zero, maximum ya minimum hota hai; beech ke points se curve aur saaf banta hai. Table bana kar points plot karenge aur unhein haath se smooth curve (narm, gol mor wali lakeer) se jorenge, seedhi lakeeron se nahi. Ek chakkar ban jaye to poore interval mein wohi pattern dohrayenge. Graph paper par pehle scale tay karein: x-axis par har qadam (jaise pi/4 ya 1 unit) ke liye barabar khaane, aur y-axis par 1 unit ke liye munasib khaane. Axes ke naam (x, y) aur har nishan par us ki value likhna na bhoolein; exam mein examiner sab se pehle yahi dekhta hai. Agar koi point baqi lehar se hat kar aaye to us ka hisaab dobara check karein; aksar ghalti angle banane mein ya calculator ke degree mode mein hoti hai.

Amplitude, period aur chakkaron ki tadaad
\[\text{Amplitude} = |-1| = 1\]
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\]
\[\text{Cycles} = \dfrac{4\pi}{\pi} = 4\]
Kyun: sine ki value \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan rehti hai, minus lagane se bhi yeh hadd nahi badalti, is liye amplitude 1. Angle \(2x\) hai, to \(x\) ke \(\pi\) chalne par angle \(2\pi\) chal leta hai: period \(\pi\). Interval ki lambai \(2\pi - (-2\pi) = 4\pi\) hai, is mein \(\pi\) lambai ke 4 chakkar aate hain.

Ek period ke liye x-values chunein
Quarter period \(= \pi/4\); beech wale points bhi lenge, to \(x = 0, \pi/8, \pi/4, \ldots, \pi\).
Kyun: sine wave mein zero, maximum aur minimum hamesha quarter period ke faasle par aate hain. \(\pi/8\) wale beech ke points batate hain ke curve kitna gol hai.

Table ki values nikalein (table jawab ke neeche di gayi hai)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} = -1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2} = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} \approx -0.71\]
Kyun: tarteeb yaad rakhein: pehle \(x\) ko double karo (angle), phir us ka sine lo, phir sign ulta karo.
Dhyan dein: \(-\sin 2x\) ko \(\sin(-2x)\) ya \(-2\sin x\) na samjhein. Minus poore sine ke bahar hai aur 2 angle ke andar.

Negative \(x\) ki values
\[y(-x) = -\sin(-2x) = \sin 2x = -y(x)\]
\[x = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ y = 1\]
Kyun: yeh function odd hai, is liye negative \(x\) par table ki values sirf sign badal leti hain. Waise bhi pattern har \(\pi\) ke baad dohraya jata hai, to alag hisaab ki zaroorat nahi.

Plot kar ke jorein
x-axis par \(-2\pi\) se \(2\pi\) tak \(\pi/4\) ke qadam, aur y-axis par \(-1\) se \(1\) tak nishan lagayein. Points plot kar ke smooth lehar se jorein.
Curve har \(\pi/2\) ke multiple par x-axis ko kaat-ta hai; minimum \(-1\) \(x = -7\pi/4, -3\pi/4, \pi/4, 5\pi/4\) par aur maximum \(1\) \(x = -5\pi/4, -\pi/4, 3\pi/4, 7\pi/4\) par.
Kyun: \(x = 0\) se aage curve pehle neeche jata hai (minus ki wajah se), jabke \(\sin 2x\) pehle upar jata. Yahi pehchan hai ke graph sahi ulta hua hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{2}\]
\[= -(-1) = 1\]
Kyun: \(7\pi/2 = 2\pi + 3\pi/2\), aur \(\sin(3\pi/2) = -1\). Minus lagane se 1, yani aakhri maximum wahi hai jahan graph dikhata hai.
blocks.final_answer: Ulti (upside-down) sine wave, amplitude 1, period \(\pi\): \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) par 4 poore chakkar; zeros \(\pi/2\) ke har multiple par, minimum \(-1\) \(x = -7\pi/4, -3\pi/4, \pi/4, 5\pi/4\) par, maximum \(1\) \(x = -5\pi/4, -\pi/4, 3\pi/4, 7\pi/4\) par.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = -sin 2x from -2 pi to 2 pi: an upside-down sine wave of height 1 making four complete cycles, crossing the x-axis at every multiple of pi/2.
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (i): y = −sin 2x on [−2π, 2π] (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = 2\cos 2x,\ x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi graph ka sawal hai. Bahar wala 2 lehar ki unchai double karta hai, aur andar wala 2 period aadha kar deta hai. Dono ka kaam alag alag hai, inhein mix na karein.
Plan: amplitude 2, period \(\pi\); \([0, \pi]\) ki table banayenge aur \(2\pi\) tak ek dafa aur dohrayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = 2\cos 2x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Humein banana hai: is interval par graph.
Tareeqa: pehle amplitude (lehar ki unchai) aur period (ek chakkar ki lambai) nikalenge. Phir period ke chauthe hisse (quarter period) ke faasle par x-values lenge, kyunke inhi jagahon par graph zero, maximum ya minimum hota hai; beech ke points se curve aur saaf banta hai. Table bana kar points plot karenge aur unhein haath se smooth curve (narm, gol mor wali lakeer) se jorenge, seedhi lakeeron se nahi. Ek chakkar ban jaye to poore interval mein wohi pattern dohrayenge. Graph paper par pehle scale tay karein: x-axis par har qadam (jaise pi/4 ya 1 unit) ke liye barabar khaane, aur y-axis par 1 unit ke liye munasib khaane. Axes ke naam (x, y) aur har nishan par us ki value likhna na bhoolein; exam mein examiner sab se pehle yahi dekhta hai. Agar koi point baqi lehar se hat kar aaye to us ka hisaab dobara check karein; aksar ghalti angle banane mein ya calculator ke degree mode mein hoti hai.

Amplitude, period aur chakkar
\[\text{Amplitude} = 2\]
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\]
\[\text{Cycles} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2\]
Kyun: \(\cos 2x\) hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hai; 2 se multiply karne par \(-2\) aur \(2\) ke darmiyan ho jata hai. Angle \(2x\) hai, is liye period \(2\pi/2 = \pi\), aur \(2\pi\) lambe interval mein do chakkar.

x-values chunein
Quarter period \(= \pi/4\); beech ke points ke saath \(x = 0, \pi/8, \ldots, \pi\).
Kyun: cosine wave mein maximum, zero, minimum, zero, maximum: yeh paanch khaas points quarter period ke faasle par aate hain.

Table ki values nikalein
\[x = 0:\ y = 2\cos 0 = 2\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}:\ y = 2\cos\pi = -2\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} \approx 1.41\]
Kyun: pehle \(x\) double kar ke angle banaya, phir cosine liya, phir 2 se multiply kiya. \([\pi, 2\pi]\) ke liye yahi values dobara aati hain, kyunke period \(\pi\) hai.
Dhyan dein: \(2\cos 2x\) ko \(\cos 4x\) na samjhein; 2 bahar multiply hai, angle ke andar nahi jata.

Plot kar ke jorein
x-axis par \(0\) se \(2\pi\) tak \(\pi/4\) ke qadam aur y-axis par \(-2\) se \(2\) tak nishan lagayein. Points ko smooth lehar se jorein.
Maximum \(2\): \(x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\); minimum \(-2\): \(x = \pi/2, 3\pi/2\); zeros: \(x = \pi/4, 3\pi/4, 5\pi/4, 7\pi/4\).
Kyun: cosine wave hamesha apne maximum se shuru hoti hai, is liye graph unchai 2 se shuru ho kar unchai 2 par hi khatam hota hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}:\ y = 2\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{2} = 0\]
Kyun: \(7\pi/2 = 2\pi + 3\pi/2\) aur \(\cos(3\pi/2) = 0\). Aakhri zero \(7\pi/4\) par hai, bilkul graph ke mutabiq.
blocks.final_answer: Cosine wave, amplitude 2, period \(\pi\): \([0, 2\pi]\) par 2 poore chakkar; maximum \(2\) \(x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\) par, minimum \(-2\) \(x = \pi/2, 3\pi/2\) par, zeros \(x = \pi/4, 3\pi/4, 5\pi/4, 7\pi/4\) par.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = 2 cos 2x from 0 to 2 pi: a cosine wave of height 2 making two complete cycles, maxima 2 at 0, pi and 2 pi, minima -2 at pi/2 and 3 pi/2.
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (ii): y = 2 cos 2x on [0, 2π] (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \tan 2x,\ x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh tangent ka graph hai. Tangent ki koi unchai ki hadd nahi: is ka koi maximum ya minimum nahi hota, lekin jahan \(\tan 2x\) undefined ho wahan khari asymptote lines aati hain jinhein graph kabhi chhoota nahi.
Plan: period aur asymptotes nikalenge, ek branch (shaakh) ki table banayenge, phir usi branch ko har period ke baad dohrayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \tan 2x\), \(x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
Humein banana hai: is interval par graph.
Tareeqa: \(\tan cx\) ka period \(\pi/c\) hota hai. Asymptotes wahan hain jahan angle \(\pi/2\) ka odd multiple ho. Ek branch table se banayenge aur phir har period ke baad copy karenge. Sine aur cosine ki tarah yahan amplitude nahi hota, is liye y-axis par range khud chunni parti hai, jaise \(-4\) se \(4\).

Period
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: tangent \(\pi\) ke baad dohraya jata hai, \(2\pi\) ke baad nahi, aur angle \(2x\) hai jo \(x\) se double tez chalta hai. Is liye \(\pi \div 2\).

Khari asymptotes
\[2x = \pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\]
\[x = \pm\dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\tan\theta = \sin\theta/\cos\theta\), aur jahan \(\cos\theta = 0\) ho wahan zero se divide hota hai, yani value mojood hi nahi. Yeh \(\theta = \pm\pi/2, \pm3\pi/2\) par hota hai. Wahan dashed khari lakeerein kheenchein.
Dhyan dein: asymptote ko curve ka hissa na samjhein aur curve ko us ke paar na jorein; har branch alag hai.

Zeros
\[2x = 0,\ \pm\pi,\ \pm2\pi\]
\[x = 0,\ \pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \pm\pi\]
Kyun: \(\tan\theta = 0\) wahan hota hai jahan \(\sin\theta = 0\), yani \(\theta\) \(\pi\) ka multiple ho.

Beech wali branch ki table
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{3} \approx 1.73\]
\[x = -\dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = -1\]
Kyun: tangent odd hai, is liye negative taraf wohi values minus ke saath aati hain. Jaise jaise \(x\) \(\pi/4\) ke qareeb jata hai, value bohat bari hoti jati hai (\(+\infty\) ki taraf); \(-\pi/4\) ke qareeb bohat neeche (\(-\infty\) ki taraf).

Dohrayein aur graph banayein
Branch ko har \(\pi/2\) ke baad copy karein: poori branches \((-3\pi/4, -\pi/4)\), \((-\pi/4, \pi/4)\), \((\pi/4, 3\pi/4)\) par, aur aadhi branches \([-\pi, -3\pi/4)\) aur \((3\pi/4, \pi]\) par.
Kyun: \([-\pi, \pi]\) ki lambai \(2\pi\) hai, yani 4 periods. Dono kinaron wale aadhe tukre mil kar chauthi branch banate hain. Har branch left se right upar charhti hai aur asymptotes ko kabhi nahi chhooti.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \dfrac{7\pi}{8}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{7\pi}{4} = -1\]
Kyun: \(7\pi/8\) right wali aadhi branch par hai, jo \(3\pi/4\) par \(-\infty\) se shuru ho kar \(\pi\) par 0 tak aati hai. \(-1\) bilkul is raaste par hai.
blocks.final_answer: Period \(\pi/2\) wali tangent branches, har ek left se right upar charhti hui; khari asymptotes \(x = \pm\pi/4, \pm3\pi/4\), zeros \(x = 0, \pm\pi/2, \pm\pi\): \([-\pi, \pi]\) par teen poori aur kinaron par do aadhi branches.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = tan 2x from -pi to pi: rising tangent branches separated by dashed vertical asymptotes at x = -3pi/4, -pi/4, pi/4, 3pi/4, crossing the x-axis at -pi, -pi/2, 0, pi/2, pi.
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (iii): y = tan 2x on [−π, π] with asymptotes dashed (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \tan \frac{x}{2},\ x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi tangent ka graph hai, lekin angle aadha (\(x/2\)) hai. Angle aadha hone se graph daayen baayen phail jata hai aur period double ho jata hai.
Plan: period aur asymptotes nikalenge, table banayenge, phir \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) par branches kheenchenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \tan\frac{x}{2}\), \(x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
Humein banana hai: is interval par graph.
Tareeqa: \(\tan cx\) ka period \(\pi/c\). Asymptotes wahan jahan angle \(\pi/2\) ka odd multiple ho. Phir table, plot aur smooth branches. Tangent mein amplitude nahi hota, is liye y-axis par munasib range (jaise \(-4\) se \(4\)) khud chunein.

Period
\[\text{Period} = \pi \div \dfrac{1}{2} = 2\pi\]
Kyun: angle \(x/2\) \(x\) ki aadhi raftaar se chalta hai. Angle ko tangent ka ek period \(\pi\) chalne ke liye \(x\) ko \(2\pi\) chalna parta hai. \(\div \tfrac12\) ka matlab \(\times 2\).

Asymptotes aur zeros
\[\dfrac{x}{2} = \pm\dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = \pm\pi\]
\[\dfrac{x}{2} = 0, \pm\pi \Rightarrow x = 0, \pm2\pi\]
Kyun: jab \(x\) \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) mein chalta hai to angle \(x/2\) sirf \([-\pi, \pi]\) mein chalta hai. Is mein \(\pi/2\) ke odd multiples sirf \(\pm\pi/2\) hain, is liye do hi asymptotes \(x = \pm\pi\).

Table ki values
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1\]
\[x = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{3} \approx 1.73\]
Kyun: pehle \(x\) ko aadha karo, phir tangent lo. \(3\pi/4\) doosre quadrant (Quadrant II) mein hai jahan tangent negative hota hai, is liye \(-1\). Negative \(x\) par wohi values ulte sign ke saath, kyunke tangent odd hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\tan(x/2)\) ko \(\tfrac12\tan x\) na samjhein; aadha angle ka hai, jawab ka nahi.

Branches kheenchein
\((-\pi, \pi)\) par origin se guzarti poori branch, \(-\infty\) se \(+\infty\) tak upar charhti hui; \((\pi, 2\pi]\) par aadhi branch, \(-\infty\) se 0 tak; \([-2\pi, -\pi)\) par aadhi branch, 0 se \(+\infty\) tak.
Kyun: interval ki lambai \(4\pi\) hai, yani 2 periods: ek poori branch aur do aadhi, jo mil kar doosri branch banati hain.

Tasdeeq
\[x = -\dfrac{3\pi}{2}:\ y = \tan\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) = 1\]
Kyun: left wali aadhi branch \((-2\pi, 0)\) se shuru ho kar asymptote \(x = -\pi\) ki taraf upar jati hai. \(-3\pi/2\) par value 1 isi raaste par hai.
blocks.final_answer: Period \(2\pi\) wali tangent branches; khari asymptotes \(x = \pm\pi\), zeros \(x = -2\pi, 0, 2\pi\): \((-\pi, \pi)\) par ek poori upar charhti branch aur \([-2\pi, -\pi)\) aur \((\pi, 2\pi]\) par aadhi branches.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = tan(x/2) from -2 pi to 2 pi: a full rising branch between dashed asymptotes x = -pi and x = pi through the origin, and half branches on [-2 pi, -pi) and (pi, 2 pi].
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (iv): y = tan(x/2) on [−2π, 2π] with asymptotes dashed (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (v) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \sin \frac{\pi}{2}x,\ x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein \(x\) ke coefficient mein khud \(\pi\) hai, is liye period saada number nikalta hai aur x-axis par 0, 1, 2, ... jaise aam numbers lagte hain, \(\pi/4\) wale nahi.
Plan: period 4, 0.5 ke qadam se table, aur \(2\pi \approx 6.28\) tak plot.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sin\frac{\pi}{2}x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Humein banana hai: is interval par graph.
Tareeqa: pehle amplitude (lehar ki unchai) aur period (ek chakkar ki lambai) nikalenge. Phir period ke chauthe hisse (quarter period) ke faasle par x-values lenge, kyunke inhi jagahon par graph zero, maximum ya minimum hota hai; beech ke points se curve aur saaf banta hai. Table bana kar points plot karenge aur unhein haath se smooth curve (narm, gol mor wali lakeer) se jorenge, seedhi lakeeron se nahi. Ek chakkar ban jaye to poore interval mein wohi pattern dohrayenge. Graph paper par pehle scale tay karein: x-axis par har qadam (jaise pi/4 ya 1 unit) ke liye barabar khaane, aur y-axis par 1 unit ke liye munasib khaane. Axes ke naam (x, y) aur har nishan par us ki value likhna na bhoolein; exam mein examiner sab se pehle yahi dekhta hai. Agar koi point baqi lehar se hat kar aaye to us ka hisaab dobara check karein; aksar ghalti angle banane mein ya calculator ke degree mode mein hoti hai.

Amplitude, period aur chakkar
\[\text{Amplitude} = 1\]
\[\text{Period} = 2\pi \div \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 4\]
\[\text{Cycles} = \dfrac{2\pi}{4} \approx 1.57\]
Kyun: \(2\pi \times 2/\pi = 4\), dono \(\pi\) cancel ho gaye. Interval \(2\pi \approx 6.28\) lamba hai, is mein 4 lambai ka ek poora chakkar, phir aadha, aur thora sa mazeed aata hai.

x-values chunein
Quarter period \(= 1\); beech ke points ke saath \(x = 0, 0.5, 1, \ldots, 6\) aur aakhri point \(x = 2\pi\).
Kyun: zeros aur peaks 1 unit ke faasle par aate hain; 0.5 wale points curve ki golai dikhate hain. Interval \(2\pi\) par khatam hota hai, 6 par nahi, is liye aakhri point alag se lena zaroori hai.

Table ki values nikalein
\[x = 2.5:\ \sin\dfrac{5\pi}{4} = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} \approx -0.71\]
\[x = 2\pi:\ \sin(\pi^2) \approx \sin 9.87\]
\[\approx -0.43\]
Kyun: \(x\) ko \(\pi/2\) se multiply kar ke angle banaya. \(5\pi/4\) teesre quadrant mein hai jahan sine negative hai. Aakhri angle \(\pi^2\) koi standard angle nahi, is liye calculator radian mode mein rakh kar value li.
Dhyan dein: calculator degree mode mein ho to \(\sin 9.87\) ghalat aayega. Jab angle mein \(\pi\) na ho ya saada number ho, radian mode zaroori hai.

Plot kar ke jorein
x-axis par aam numbers \(0\) se \(6\) (aur \(2\pi \approx 6.28\)), y-axis par \(-1\) se \(1\). Points ko smooth lehar se jorein.
Zeros \(x = 0, 2, 4, 6\) par; maximum \(1\) \(x = 1, 5\) par; minimum \(-1\) \(x = 3\) par; curve \((2\pi, -0.43)\) par khatam hota hai.
Kyun: har sine wave ki tarah yeh origin se shuru ho kar pehle upar jati hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 5:\ \sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2} = \sin\left(2\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1\]
Kyun: \(5 = 1 + 4\), yani pehle maximum se theek ek period baad; is liye yahan bhi maximum hai.
blocks.final_answer: Sine wave, amplitude 1, period 4: zeros \(x = 0, 2, 4, 6\) par, maximum \(1\) \(x = 1, 5\) par, minimum \(-1\) \(x = 3\) par, aakhri point \((2\pi, -0.43)\); \([0, 2\pi]\) par taqreeban \(1\tfrac12\) chakkar.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = sin(pi x / 2) from 0 to 2 pi: a sine wave of height 1 and period 4, maxima at x = 1 and 5, minimum at x = 3, zeros at 0, 2, 4, 6, ending at (2 pi, -0.43).
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (v): y = sin(πx/2) on [0, 2π]; x marked in ordinary numbers (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \cos \frac{\pi}{2}x,\ x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh cosine ka graph hai jis ka period saada number hai. Cosine even hai, is liye graph y-axis ke gird aaine (mirror) ki tarah symmetric hoga.
Plan: period 4, \(x \ge 0\) ki table, aur \(x < 0\) ke liye usi ka aaina.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \cos\frac{\pi}{2}x\), \(x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
Humein banana hai: is interval par graph.
Tareeqa: pehle amplitude (lehar ki unchai) aur period (ek chakkar ki lambai) nikalenge. Phir period ke chauthe hisse (quarter period) ke faasle par x-values lenge, kyunke inhi jagahon par graph zero, maximum ya minimum hota hai; beech ke points se curve aur saaf banta hai. Table bana kar points plot karenge aur unhein haath se smooth curve (narm, gol mor wali lakeer) se jorenge, seedhi lakeeron se nahi. Ek chakkar ban jaye to poore interval mein wohi pattern dohrayenge. Graph paper par pehle scale tay karein: x-axis par har qadam (jaise pi/4 ya 1 unit) ke liye barabar khaane, aur y-axis par 1 unit ke liye munasib khaane. Axes ke naam (x, y) aur har nishan par us ki value likhna na bhoolein; exam mein examiner sab se pehle yahi dekhta hai. Agar koi point baqi lehar se hat kar aaye to us ka hisaab dobara check karein; aksar ghalti angle banane mein ya calculator ke degree mode mein hoti hai.

Amplitude aur period
\[\text{Amplitude} = 1\]
\[\text{Period} = 2\pi \div \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 4\]
Kyun: \(\pi\) cancel ho gaya, period 4. Interval \([-\pi, \pi]\) ki lambai \(2\pi \approx 6.28\) hai, yani taqreeban dairh (one and a half) period.

\(x \ge 0\) ki table
\[x = 1:\ \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 0\]
\[x = 2:\ \cos\pi = -1\]
\[x = \pi:\ \cos\dfrac{\pi^2}{2} \approx \cos 4.93\]
\[\approx 0.22\]
Kyun: 4.93 radian \(3\pi/2 \approx 4.71\) se thora zyada hai, yani chauthe quadrant (Quadrant IV) mein, jahan cosine positive hota hai. Is liye 0.22 positive hai. Calculator radian mode mein.
Dhyan dein: kinare par \(x = \pi\) hai, 3 nahi. Bohat se students graph 3 par rok dete hain; aakhri chhota sa hissa \(3\) se \(\pi\) tak bhi banana hai.

\(x < 0\) ki values
\[\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\right) = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\]
Kyun: cosine even hai, to \(-x\) par wohi \(y\) jo \(x\) par. Is liye left aadha right aadhe ka aaina hai; dobara hisaab ki zaroorat nahi.

Plot kar ke jorein
x-axis par aam numbers \(-3\) se \(3\) (aur \(\pm\pi\)), y-axis par \(-1\) se \(1\). Smooth lehar se jorein.
Maximum \(1\) \(x = 0\) par; minimum \(-1\) \(x = \pm2\) par; zeros \(x = \pm1, \pm3\) par; dono kinare \((\pm\pi, 0.22)\).
Kyun: cosine wave ki choti 0 par hoti hai aur dono taraf neeche girti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 3:\ \cos\dfrac{3\pi}{2} = 0\]
Kyun: cosine wave mein minimum ke dono taraf quarter period (yahan 1) ke faasle par zeros hote hain: \(2 \pm 1 = 1, 3\). Bilkul table ke mutabiq.
blocks.final_answer: Cosine wave, amplitude 1, period 4, y-axis ke gird symmetric: maximum \(1\) \(x = 0\) par, minimum \(-1\) \(x = \pm2\) par, zeros \(x = \pm1, \pm3\) par, kinare \((\pm\pi, 0.22)\).
